pr_title: Kubectl certificate signing: fix certificate deny message
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**

/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

Fixes an incorrect message when manually denying a certificate signing request
Currently, denied CSRs are getting an **approved** message
```bash
$ kubectl certificate deny mycert
certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/mycert approved
```

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #84398

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

Find at the lined issue instructions for reproducing the issue 

```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: Kubectl returning wrong message for CSR deny
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
Denying a certificate signing requests show a message indicating that the requests was approved

```bash
$ kubectl certificate deny mycert
certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/mycert approved
```

**What you expected to happen**:
A denial message would be expected

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
After generating a CSR, create the `CertificateSigningRequest`

```bash
$ cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: mycsr
spec:
  request: $(cat my.csr)
  usages:
  - server auth
EOF

$ kubectl get csr
NAME                    AGE    REQUESTOR       CONDITION
mycsr                   12s    minikube-user   Pending
```

Deny the certificate request manually
```bash
$ kubectl certificate deny mycsr
certificatesigningrequest.certificates.k8s.io/mycsr approved
```
Notice the **approved** message

The request is denied as expected, the issue only affects the deny operation returning message
```bash
$ kubectl get csr
mycsr                   1m6s   minikube-user   Denied
```

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.16
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): linux
- Install tools: minikube

review_comments: Rather than dropping this, add the operation to the signature. This helps consumers of this command understand all the inputs required to construct the options

@liggitt  thanks for the review.

`NewCertificateOptions` is back
